# Systems and frameworks

[Overview](../README.md) · [Research papers](papers.md) · [Filter systems in the explorer](https://duyvuleo.github.io/awesome-agents-that-learn/?kind=system#catalog)

23 software records. Catalog updated: 2026-10-30; individual inspection dates are recorded per entry. Systems are counted separately from the 129 research works; a paper and its software can describe the same research program. These are documentation/source inspections, not installations, reproductions, or deployment endorsements. No release date is inferred from the review date.

<a id="system-a-mem"></a>

## A-MEM memory system

**Memory library · core · source inspected · not run**

[Official repository](https://github.com/WujiangXu/A-mem-sys)

**Learning mechanism.** Builds structured memory notes, indexes them in ChromaDB, and links or revises related memories as new information arrives. This adapts the external memory organization.

**Capabilities.** Structured note generation; Memory linking; Configurable model backends

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** New memory content, model-generated context/tags, and similarity to existing notes.

**Paper relationship.** The authors distinguish this reusable memory-system repository from the separate AgenticMemory repository used for paper-result reproduction.

[A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents](papers.md#a-mem)

**Evaluation evidence.** The README refers to paper comparisons but directs reproduction work to a different evaluation repository.

**Boundary.** Current library functionality is not proof that the paper’s evaluation has been reproduced. The agent and persistent-memory policy still need application-specific integration.

**Availability.** Public reusable memory-library source; package installation documented; not installed or run.

**Requirements.** Python dependencies, ChromaDB/embedding support, and an OpenAI, Ollama, SGLang, or OpenRouter backend as documented.

**License.** [MIT](https://github.com/WujiangXu/A-mem-sys/blob/main/LICENSE). Linked models, datasets, services, and dependencies can have separate terms.

**Source inspection:** 2026-10-28 · project · not-run. **Topics:** memory, continual-learning.

[Source 1](https://github.com/WujiangXu/A-mem-sys) · [Source 2](https://github.com/WujiangXu/A-mem-sys/blob/main/LICENSE)


<a id="system-absolute-zero"></a>

## Absolute Zero Reasoner

**Research implementation · core · source inspected · not run**

[Official repository](https://github.com/LeapLabTHU/Absolute-Zero-Reasoner) · [Documentation](https://github.com/LeapLabTHU/Absolute-Zero-Reasoner/blob/master/README.md)

**Learning mechanism.** Implements reinforced self-play in which a model proposes reasoning tasks and solves them with execution-based verification. Updated weights and a generated task pool support later training iterations.

**Capabilities.** Generate and validate code-based reasoning tasks; Run proposer/solver self-play training; Use linked evaluation code, checkpoints, and experiment logs

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Python execution validates generated tasks and answers and supplies proposer/solver rewards.

**Paper relationship.** Official Absolute Zero Reasoner release. The README points to a separate paper branch for original-result replication; the moving development code should not be assumed equivalent.

[Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data](papers.md#absolute-zero)

**Evaluation evidence.** The paper reports coding and mathematics benchmarks; the repository provides training/evaluation resources and distinguishes its paper branch. No checkpoint or training run was tested here.

**Boundary.** The README labels newer development changes as under testing and the raw executor as research-only. Zero newly curated task data does not remove pretraining or engineered supervision.

**Availability.** Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.

**Requirements.** GPU training environment with veRL and pretrained weights; documented model-size configurations use multiple 80 GB GPUs. A sandbox executor option requires Docker.

**License.** [MIT](https://github.com/LeapLabTHU/Absolute-Zero-Reasoner/blob/master/LICENSE). Linked models, datasets, services, and dependencies can have separate terms.

**Source inspection:** 2026-10-28 · project · not-run. **Topics:** model-training, self-play.

<a id="system-adas"></a>

## ADAS / Meta Agent Search

**Research implementation · core · source inspected · not run**

[Official repository](https://github.com/ShengranHu/ADAS) · [Documentation](https://github.com/ShengranHu/ADAS/blob/main/README.md)

**Learning mechanism.** A fixed meta-agent search procedure writes candidate agent programs, evaluates them, and consults earlier discoveries when proposing new designs. Domain-specific evaluators determine which designs are useful.

**Capabilities.** Search code-represented agent designs; Retain evaluated discoveries in an archive; Adapt domain-specific search and scoring functions

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Benchmark evaluation and an archive of previously generated agent designs.

**Paper relationship.** Official research implementation of Automated Design of Agentic Systems and its Meta Agent Search algorithm; benchmark folders contain separate experiment setups.

[Automated Design of Agentic Systems](papers.md#adas)

**Evaluation evidence.** The paper reports task and model transfer experiments; the repository documents how to run the domain studies. No search run was executed here.

**Boundary.** The search procedure is externally configured rather than itself established as an evolving optimizer. The repository explicitly notes that it executes model-generated code.

**Availability.** Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.

**Requirements.** Python 3.11 environment, required dependencies, model access, and the selected domain’s data and evaluation setup.

**License.** [Apache-2.0](https://github.com/ShengranHu/ADAS/blob/main/LICENSE). Linked models, datasets, services, and dependencies can have separate terms.

**Source inspection:** 2026-10-28 · project · not-run. **Topics:** architecture, workflows, prompts.

<a id="system-aflow"></a>

## AFlow

**Research implementation · core · source inspected · not run**

[Official repository](https://github.com/FoundationAgents/AFlow) · [Documentation](https://github.com/FoundationAgents/AFlow/blob/main/README.md)

**Learning mechanism.** Searches code-represented workflows using a Monte Carlo tree-search variant over configurable operators. An evaluator scores candidate workflows and guides later prompt and structure changes.

**Capabilities.** Search and evaluate agent workflows; Customize operators and benchmark interfaces; Inspect released workflow and validation traces

**What changes:** Workflows, Prompts / context, Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Validation-set execution scores and retained search history.

**Paper relationship.** Official standalone AFlow repository, migrated from MetaGPT; it implements the workflow-search method associated with the paper.

[AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation](papers.md#aflow)

**Evaluation evidence.** The project provides evaluation code and experiment artifacts for QA, coding, and mathematics tasks; the collection has not rerun them.

**Boundary.** The README warns that some operators may contain migration bugs. Repeated validation use and search cost must be separated from the selected workflow’s test performance and inference cost.

**Availability.** Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.

**Requirements.** Documented Python 3.9 environment, model configuration, benchmark data, and task operators/evaluator.

**License.** [MIT](https://github.com/FoundationAgents/AFlow/blob/main/LICENSE). Linked models, datasets, services, and dependencies can have separate terms.

**Source inspection:** 2026-10-28 · project · not-run. **Topics:** workflows, architecture, prompts.

<a id="system-agent-lightning"></a>

## Agent Lightning v1.0

**Training framework · core · source inspected · not run**

[Official repository](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-lightning) · [Documentation](https://microsoft.github.io/agent-lightning/stable/00-installation/)

**Learning mechanism.** Separates policy training, model-request interception, and agent rollout execution through a trainer, API gateway, and controller. Captured interactions become training samples while the agent retains its tool and control-flow environment.

**Capabilities.** Train policies using real agent harnesses; Collect model interactions through an API gateway; Run rollouts locally or as Kubernetes jobs

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task rewards and trajectories collected from agents running their existing harnesses.

**Paper relationship.** Official Microsoft agent-training framework. Its v1.0 technical report is linked by the project but is not yet a separate literature entry in this catalog; legacy v0.x is maintained on another branch.

No associated work in the current paper catalog.

**Evaluation evidence.** Project documentation reports search, sandbox, and coding-agent examples. These are project-reported results, not measurements performed or reproduced by this collection.

**Boundary.** This is externally configured training infrastructure, not proof of autonomous self-directed improvement. The v1.0 architecture is a documented refactor, so v0.x installation and experiment assumptions should not be transferred automatically.

**Availability.** Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.

**Requirements.** NVIDIA CUDA and a compatible verl/vLLM/PyTorch training stack; current setup docs describe W&B logging and local or Kubernetes rollout environments.

**License.** [MIT](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-lightning/blob/main/LICENSE). Linked models, datasets, services, and dependencies can have separate terms.

**Source inspection:** 2026-10-28 · project · not-run. **Topics:** model-training, tools, workflows, evaluation.

## Agent0

**Research implementation · core · source inspected · not run**

[Official repository](https://github.com/aiming-lab/Agent0) · [Documentation](https://github.com/aiming-lab/Agent0/blob/main/Agent0/README.md)

**Learning mechanism.** Alternates curriculum generation, task filtering, and reinforcement-learning updates of a tool-using executor. A deployed code sandbox supplies execution for multi-turn training trajectories.

**Capabilities.** Train a tool-aware curriculum agent; Filter generated tasks using self-consistency; Train an executor through multi-turn RL

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Curriculum rewards, tool interactions, and self-consistency-filtered executor training data.

**Paper relationship.** The official repository now hosts the Agent0 series, including a separate vision-language project. This entry describes the Agent0 language-agent subdirectory linked to the cataloged paper.

[Agent0: Unleashing Self-Evolving Agents from Zero Data via Tool-Integrated Reasoning](papers.md#agent0)

**Evaluation evidence.** The paper and repository report reasoning benchmarks for particular trained models. This catalog did not run training or evaluate a released checkpoint.

**Boundary.** Zero data excludes new human-curated task labels, not pretrained weights, reward design, or tools. The documented workflow includes manual checkpoint selection between iterations.

**Availability.** Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.

**Requirements.** Training-capable hardware, the documented veRL-based environment, pretrained model weights, and a configured SandboxFusion service.

**License.** [Apache-2.0](https://github.com/aiming-lab/Agent0/blob/main/LICENSE). Linked models, datasets, services, and dependencies can have separate terms.

**Source inspection:** 2026-10-28 · project · not-run. **Topics:** model-training, self-play, tools.

## Darwin Gödel Machine

**Research implementation · core · source inspected · not run**

[Official repository](https://github.com/jennyzzt/dgm) · [Documentation](https://github.com/jennyzzt/dgm/blob/main/README.md)

**Learning mechanism.** Runs a coding agent on changes to its own implementation and retains evaluated variants in an archive. Later iterations can build on earlier variants rather than only the most recent agent.

**Capabilities.** Generate and evaluate self-edits to agent code; Maintain an archive of candidate agents; Inspect SWE-bench and Polyglot experiment artifacts

**What changes:** Agent code, Tools, Workflows, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Coding-benchmark outcomes and logs from candidate agent variants.

**Paper relationship.** Official DGM research code, with separate SWE-bench and Polyglot evaluation components and linked experiment logs; current source was not matched to a paper-run commit.

[Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents](papers.md#darwin-godel-machine)

**Evaluation evidence.** The related paper reports coding evaluations and ablations; the repository exposes the research loop and experiment logs. No result was independently reproduced here.

**Boundary.** The outer selection/evaluation process and foundation models remain fixed in the inspected study. The repository executes generated code and is a research implementation, not a validated general deployment service.

**Availability.** Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.

**Requirements.** Python dependencies, Docker, configured model access, and benchmark environment/data preparation.

**License.** [Apache-2.0](https://github.com/jennyzzt/dgm/blob/main/LICENSE). Linked models, datasets, services, and dependencies can have separate terms.

**Source inspection:** 2026-10-28 · project · not-run. **Topics:** architecture, recursive-improvement, applications.

<a id="system-dspy"></a>

## DSPy

**Optimization framework · core · source inspected · not run**

[Official repository](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy) · [Documentation](https://dspy.ai/)

**Learning mechanism.** Builds language-model applications from typed signatures and composable Python modules. Optimizers can produce reusable prompts, demonstrations, or tuned model parameters for a supplied task and metric.

**Capabilities.** Compose reasoning, retrieval, and tool-using modules; Optimize instructions and demonstrations against a metric; Use optional fine-tuning optimizers

**What changes:** Prompts / context, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Developer-supplied examples and metrics, with feedback or fine-tuning objectives determined by the chosen optimizer.

**Paper relationship.** Official DSPy framework; the original paper and GEPA describe particular optimization methods, not every capability of the current release.

[DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines](papers.md#dspy) · [GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning](papers.md#gepa)

**Evaluation evidence.** The linked papers report evaluations of specific optimizers; current framework documentation supplies further application examples. This catalog does not test the latest release.

**Boundary.** Optimization must be configured with appropriate data, metrics, and models. A compiled program does not by itself become a continuously self-learning deployed agent.

**Availability.** Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.

**Requirements.** Python 3.10 or newer, a supported language-model backend, and task examples plus an evaluation metric for optimization.

**License.** [MIT](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/main/LICENSE). Linked models, datasets, services, and dependencies can have separate terms.

**Source inspection:** 2026-10-28 · project · not-run. **Topics:** prompts, workflows, model-training, tools.

<a id="system-gepa"></a>

## GEPA

**Optimization framework · core · source inspected · not run**

[Official repository](https://github.com/gepa-ai/gepa) · [Documentation](https://gepa-ai.github.io/gepa/)

**Learning mechanism.** Uses reflection over execution feedback to propose textual edits and maintain a population of complementary candidates. Adapters connect the optimizer to prompts, program code, and other text-configured systems.

**Capabilities.** Optimize prompts through DSPy or direct adapters; Search text artifacts through optimize_anything; Track budgets, candidate history, and Pareto-based selection

**What changes:** Prompts / context, Agent code, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** User-defined evaluation scores and diagnostic traces interpreted by a reflection model.

**Paper relationship.** Official GEPA implementation; the current optimize_anything interface broadens the text-artifact optimization scope beyond the paper’s core prompt experiments.

[GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning](papers.md#gepa)

**Evaluation evidence.** The paper evaluates selected tasks and budgets; project documentation also presents demonstrations and use cases that should be assessed on their own protocols.

**Boundary.** The evaluator and search objective are externally supplied. Wider product examples do not establish the original paper’s results for every adapter or prove autonomous deployment learning.

**Availability.** Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.

**Requirements.** A Python environment, a reflection-model backend, an executable evaluation function, and examples or evaluation cases.

**License.** [MIT](https://github.com/gepa-ai/gepa/blob/main/LICENSE). Linked models, datasets, services, and dependencies can have separate terms.

**Source inspection:** 2026-10-28 · project · not-run. **Topics:** prompts, architecture, workflows, evaluation.

## Hermes Agent

**Agent application · core · source inspected · not run**

[Official repository](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) · [Documentation](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs)

**Learning mechanism.** Documents a persistent agent loop that creates and revises skills, maintains memory, and searches past sessions. Saved skills and memories remain available across later conversations.

**Capabilities.** Persistent memory and skills; Cross-session search; CLI, desktop, and messaging surfaces

**What changes:** Memory, Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Completed task experience, user interaction, periodic memory prompts, and subsequent skill use.

**Paper relationship.** Upstream Hermes application. PAST-Bench studies a Hermes baseline and an experimental Hermes+ variant; this entry is not that benchmark modification or a claim of version equivalence.

[PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents](papers.md#past-bench)

**Evaluation evidence.** Project documentation describes the learning loop; PAST-Bench provides a separate, bounded evaluation of selected Hermes configurations.

**Boundary.** Project feature claims do not establish indefinite improvement or perfect recall. Actual behavior depends on model, settings, task stream, and the inspected version.

**Availability.** Public application source with installers and desktop options; not installed or run.

**Requirements.** A supported local/hosted runtime and model-provider connection; optional cloud services have separate costs and terms.

**License.** [MIT](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/LICENSE). Linked models, datasets, services, and dependencies can have separate terms.

<a id="system-hyperagents"></a>

## HyperAgents

**Research implementation · core · source inspected · not run**

[Official repository](https://github.com/facebookresearch/HyperAgents) · [Documentation](https://github.com/facebookresearch/HyperAgents/blob/main/README.md)

**Learning mechanism.** Makes both a task-solving agent and its improvement procedure editable. A fixed outer loop runs candidate changes and evaluation across configured domains.

**Capabilities.** Modify task-agent and meta-agent programs; Run domain-specific evolution experiments; Inspect released experiment logs and analysis tools

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task evaluation and the histories of earlier agent modifications.

**Paper relationship.** Official HyperAgents implementation accompanying the Hyperagents paper; task-agent and meta-agent code are separate editable components in the released research setup.

[Hyperagents](papers.md#hyperagents)

**Evaluation evidence.** The paper reports bounded multi-domain and meta-agent transfer experiments. The repository links experiment logs; no log-level audit or evolution run was performed.

**Boundary.** The outer task/evaluation boundary remains externally specified; this is not evidence of unconstrained improvement. The source is distributed under a noncommercial share-alike license.

<a id="system-memrl"></a>

## MemRL

**Research implementation · core · source inspected · not run**

[Official repository](https://github.com/MemTensor/MemRL)

**Learning mechanism.** Combines semantic retrieval with learned utility values on episodic memories while keeping the reasoning model fixed. Useful experience can therefore influence later retrieval without parameter updates.

**Capabilities.** Two-phase memory retrieval; Runtime utility updates; Four benchmark runners

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Environment outcome feedback used to update episodic-memory utility estimates.

**Paper relationship.** Official implementation of MemRL with benchmark entry points; this is not model-weight reinforcement learning.

[MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory](papers.md#memrl)

**Evaluation evidence.** The README documents HLE, BigCodeBench, ALFWorld, and Lifelong Agent Bench evaluation entry points.

**Boundary.** Updating memory utility does not establish that the base model learned new capabilities. Feedback quality and retrieval settings remain part of the evaluated system.

**Availability.** Public Python research package with configurations and runners; not installed or run.

**Requirements.** Documented Python 3.10 setup, language-model and embedding endpoints, plus the chosen benchmark assets.

**License.** [MIT](https://github.com/MemTensor/MemRL/blob/main/LICENSE). Linked models, datasets, services, and dependencies can have separate terms.

**Source inspection:** 2026-10-28 · project · not-run. **Topics:** memory, continual-learning, evaluation.

## SEAL

**Research implementation · core · source inspected · not run**

[Official repository](https://github.com/Continual-Intelligence/SEAL) · [Documentation](https://github.com/Continual-Intelligence/SEAL/blob/main/README.md)

**Learning mechanism.** Trains a model to generate adaptation data or update directives, then evaluates the gradient-based adaptation produced by those edits. The knowledge-incorporation implementation uses temporary LoRA training and evaluation to score candidate edits.

**Capabilities.** Run knowledge-incorporation self-edit experiments; Study few-shot task adaptation; Evaluate sequences of continual self-edits

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Performance measured after applying a generated self-edit to model parameters.

**Paper relationship.** Official Self-Adapting Language Models code, with separate general-knowledge and few-shot study directories; it is an adaptation research framework rather than a general agent application.

[Self-Adapting Language Models](papers.md#seal)

**Evaluation evidence.** The paper reports knowledge and ARC adaptation studies, including retention tests. The repository contains code, data, and study documentation; these were not executed here.

**Boundary.** The related study still observes forgetting, and evaluating edits involves actual model training. The release should not be treated as a stable lifelong-learning service.

**Availability.** Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.

**Requirements.** Python 3.12 and training dependencies; the README describes experiments using two A100/H100 GPUs and requires adapting provided SLURM directives to the execution environment.

**License.** [MIT](https://github.com/Continual-Intelligence/SEAL/blob/main/LICENSE). Linked models, datasets, services, and dependencies can have separate terms.
